_comment: Shadow-oracle BOOT mutations: one deterministic edit of the oracle baseline (oracle-config.sh oracle_write_config) per row of docs/design/inventory/1.5.5-config.md section 3.1 (BOOT-P01..P41), 3.2 (BOOT-001..110), 3.3 (BOOT-120..184) and 3.4 (BOOT-W01..W42).

The recorder loads <work>/config.yaml as a YAML document, applies `op` in order, re-serializes, then runs `busbar --validate` (mode=validate), boots and waits for exit or /healthz (mode=boot), or both (mode=both). It captures exit code + stderr + stdout and diffs 1.5.5 against 1.6.0.

op vocabulary: {set: <dotted>, value} replaces/creates the node at the path; {delete: <dotted>} removes it; {raw_yaml: <text>} APPENDS the text verbatim to the serialized config.yaml (used where the edit must survive as raw text, e.g. `${VAR}` interpolation rows); {env: {VAR: value}} adds to the busbar process environment on top of oracle_env; {args: [...]} are CLI arguments passed to the busbar binary instead of / in addition to `--validate`; {providers_set: <dotted>, value} edits <work>/providers.yaml the same way `set` edits config.yaml.

Dotted paths use YAML keys verbatim; a purely numeric segment is a list index (groups.broke.limits.0 = the first limit map of group `broke`; pools.oracle-unused.members.0.weight = the first member's weight).
op: [] means `no mutation` — the baseline already exhibits the row. op: null means the row cannot be triggered from config/env/args alone; `notes` names the fixture it needs.

expect.exit: refusals exit 1 (BOOT-184 exits 2); warnings exit 0 — in boot mode `0` means the recorder reached /healthz and then stopped the process cleanly. expect.stderr_contains is a literal substring of the inventory's exact message with placeholders filled in where the mutation fixes them; expect.stdout_contains is null unless a stdout literal is load-bearing.

Baseline facts relied on: listen/admin_listen loopback; identity-providers.admin-tokens {module: admin-tokens, token: {env: BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN}}; auth {chain: [keys], signing_key: {file: <work>/signing.key}, admin_auth: [admin-tokens]}; export.metrics {module: prometheus, settings: {buffer_seconds: 60}}; groups oracle/broke; six config-side providers with api_key {env: ORACLE_UPSTREAM_KEY} (=unused); six models m-<dialect>; one pool oracle-unused [m-openai-chat]; providers.yaml catalog with protocol + base_url http://127.0.0.1:<mock>. oracle_env exports BUSBAR_CONFIG, BUSBAR_PROVIDERS, ORACLE_UPSTREAM_KEY=unused, BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN, RUST_LOG=warn.
MAX_SEMAPHORE_PERMITS = tokio::sync::Semaphore::MAX_PERMITS = usize::MAX >> 3 = 2305843009213693951 on 64-bit; the over-ceiling mutations use 2305843009213693952.

Ordering traps worth knowing: env interpolation (P02-P06) runs on the raw text BEFORE the legacy-marker detector (P41), which runs BEFORE serde parse (P01, P07-P40), which runs BEFORE config::resolve (BOOT-056 resolve twin, BOOT-074c/d/e, BOOT-101), which runs BEFORE config_validate (the rest of 3.2). A `both`-scoped row that is shadowed by an earlier stage from config.yaml is marked op: null with the reason.
